children.text: The Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) collects and retains detailed records of entries into and exits from Canada. This information is known as a Travel History Report (THR), and is required when applying for permanent residency in Canada, applying for citizenship, or in certain other cases. Any tourist who has been to Canada has the ability to access their records held by the CBSA.
The THR is an official document that shows a traveler's entry and exit dates for Canada. The CBSA retains this data for 15 years.
This document includes the following information:
The traveler's first and last name, date of birth, nationality, and gender.
The exact dates of entry and exit.
The location of the port of entry (for example, an airport or a land border crossing).
The numbers of the documents used while traveling (e.g., passport number).

page.title: What is the Border Crossing document and how is it useful?

children.text: To obtain CBSA records, you need to submit a
privacy request
. The easiest way to make the request is through the ATIP online service.
If you're requesting your own personal record, this service is completely free.
Main steps for making a request:
Use the online portal: go to the Canadian government's ATIP online request
page
Specify the information: in the request form, you must clearly state that you are requesting a Travel History Report (THR) and specify the exact time period.
Indicate Entry/Exit: if you need exit information from Canada, this must be requested specifically, as this data is limited and requires precise specification.
Identification: provide your passport or NEXUS card number and other biographical details.
Processing time: keep in mind that processing CBSA requests can take up to 30 calendar days.
Another person's records: to request another person's data, their written consent is required (e.g., form BSF745), and a fee may apply.
US data: the THR only includes records of crossings at the Canadian border. Records of entry/exit for the US must be requested separately from US Customs and Border Protection (CBP).
The Travel History Report is reliable, official confirmation of your Canadian travel history, and the CBSA has made the process of obtaining it as simple as possible through its online service.
